# Paperband guide for language models

Paperband turns Markdown into laid-out documents: a web site, fixed-size pages in HTML ("paged
HTML"), and PDF. This guide has what you need to write a working Paperband project. Version
described: 0.2.0. Source: https://github.com/noregressions/paperband

How a build works:

1. A **manifest** (`manifest.yml`) lists the Markdown sources, their order, and the outputs.
2. Each file is run through the Pebble template engine, then parsed.
3. For each output, every file becomes a **page**. A **layout** (YAML) places the page's content
   into boxes, each picking content with a CSS selector.
4. Paged outputs are measured in headless Chromium. Content that doesn't fit its box fails the
   build unless the layout's `fit:` remedies make it fit.

Paperband is strict. Unknown keys, unknown layouts, misplaced markers and content that doesn't fit
are errors, not warnings. Write only the keys this guide lists.

## A complete working project

```
pom.xml
manifest.yml
docs/01-intro.md
docs/02-install.md
layouts/chapter.yml
```

`pom.xml` (the plugin part; the `chromium` dependency is needed only for `pdf` outputs and for
measuring `paged-html`):

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>dev.noregressions.paperband</groupId>
  <artifactId>paperband-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>0.2.0</version>
  <executions>
    <execution>
      <goals><goal>build</goal></goals>
    </execution>
  </executions>
  <configuration>
    <manifest>manifest.yml</manifest>
  </configuration>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>dev.noregressions.paperband</groupId>
      <artifactId>chromium</artifactId>
      <version>0.2.0</version>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</plugin>
```

The goal runs in the `generate-resources` phase: `mvn generate-resources`. It needs Java 21 and
Maven 3.9 or later.

`manifest.yml`:

```yaml
title: My guide
sources: [docs/**/*.md]
sequence:
  - files: docs/*.md
    layout: chapter
outputs:
  - { name: site, format: web, file: target/site/index.html }
  - { name: book, format: pdf, file: target/book.pdf }
```

`layouts/chapter.yml`:

```yaml
page: { size: A4, margin: 18mm }
boxes:
  - { id: title, select: h1, pick: first }
  - id: body
    select: rest
    split: true
```

`docs/01-intro.md`:

```markdown
---
title: Introduction
---
# Introduction

This guide gets you started. {! lede}

## What you need

- Java 21
- Maven
```

`docs/02-install.md`:

```markdown
# Install

Download the archive and unpack it.
```

## The manifest

Paths are relative to the manifest's directory. Every key:

```yaml
title: Paperband Guide               # default: Site
theme: forest                        # a bundled theme by name, or a theme directory (themes/mine)
stylesheets: [styles/site.css]       # inlined into every output, after the theme
templates: templates                 # Pebble include/extends directory (default: templates)
layouts: layouts                     # layout files (default: layouts)
data: data                           # YAML/JSON data, or a list of files/directories (default: data)
vars: { product: Paperband }         # template variables; single values only
env: [CI]                            # environment variables exposed to templates as env.NAME
index: index.yml                     # index terms found by rule; markers work without it
copy: [bash]                         # web: code blocks in these fence languages get a Copy button
browser: chrome                      # pdf: chrome, msedge, or a path; default: a downloaded Chromium

sources: [docs/**/*.md]              # parsed, and visible to templates through `site`
hidden: [docs/partials/*.md]         # sources deliberately not in the sequence
unused: warn                         # warn | error | ignore: sources neither in sequence nor hidden

defaults:
  page: { size: A4, margin: 15mm }
  layout: default

sequence:                            # the pages, in order
  - layout: contents                 # a generated page: a layout with no source file
  - file: docs/intro.md
  - files: docs/chapters/*.md
    where: { draft: { ne: true } }
    sort: page.chapter
    layout: chapter                  # overrides the files' own layout: front matter

outputs:
  - name: handbook                   # starts with a letter; letters, digits, -; unique
    format: paged-html               # web | paged-html | pdf
    file: build/handbook.html
    layout: print-page               # layout for pages whose sequence entry names none
    layouts: { hero: hero-print }    # or: replace layouts by name (not with layout)
    page: { size: A4, margin: 15mm }
    sequence: [...]                  # this output's own pages; default: the manifest's
    prefer: short                    # which variant to show: full | short | shortest
    single: true                     # web only: one HTML file instead of a page per file
    nav: side                        # web only: side (default) | top | none
    contents: docs/contents.md       # web only: the page shown as the navigation
```

Rules:

- `sources` and `sequence` are required, unless you use `files: [a.md, b.md]`, which is both at
  once. Don't combine `files` with `sources` or `sequence`.
- Without `outputs`, there is one web output written to `output:` (default `site.html`). Don't use
  `output` and `outputs` together.
- A `sources` pattern that matches no file is an error.
- A source that is neither in the sequence nor in `hidden` produces a warning.
- `where` operators: `eq ne gt gte lt lte in contains exists`. A bare value means equals. Keys are
  front matter keys, dotted for nested values.
- `sort` keys are `path` or `page.<front matter key>`. A file missing the key is an error unless
  you write `sort: { by: page.date, missing: last }`.
- Page sizes: `A3 A4 A5 letter legal "16:9" "4:3"`, or `{ width: 254mm, height: 143mm }`. Quote
  ratios: YAML reads an unquoted `16:9` as a number. Lengths take `mm cm in pt px`.
  `orientation: landscape` swaps width and height.

Every manifest key can also be set in the plugin's `<configuration>` (for example `<title>`,
`<theme>`, `<outputs><output>...`). A setting there overrides the manifest's.

## Markdown

CommonMark, plus GitHub pipe tables, YAML front matter, markers, fenced divs and variants.

Front matter is a YAML block at the top of the file between `---` lines. Paperband reads `layout`
(a layout name, or an inline layout as a mapping) and `id` (for links from other pages). Templates
read everything else as `page.<key>`.

### Markers

A marker `{! ...}` attaches classes, an id and values to an element, so layouts and CSS can select
it. Inside a marker: bare words are classes, `id=name` is the id, `key=value` becomes `data-key`.

````markdown
### A heading {! step id=download level=beginner}
A paragraph. {! instruction}
{! checklist}
- a list tagged by the marker on the line above
```bash {! command}
Click [Save]{! ui}, run `make`{! cmd}, see [docs](u){! external}
::: {! note}
A fenced div: any blocks grouped under one marker.
:::
````

Where a marker may go:

- at the end of a heading or paragraph, after a space
- on a line of its own, tagging the block directly below
- after a code fence's language
- straight after `[text]`, a code span, a link, an image or emphasis, with no space
- on a `:::` line, opening a fenced div closed by `:::`

A marker anywhere else is an error. Write `\{!` for a literal `{!`. Ids must be unique in a file.
A marker on a heading also applies to the heading's whole section, so `.step` selects the heading
and everything under it.

Markers with a built-in meaning:

- `{! optional}` or `{! optional priority=2}`: a block that a `drop: optional` remedy may leave out
- `{! break=force}`, `{! break=prefer}`, `{! break=avoid}`: page breaks in a splitting box
- `{! keep}` on a div: never break inside it
- `{! index}` or `{! index="term!subentry; other term"}`: an index entry
- `{! template}` after a fence's language: run the code block through the template engine

### Variants

The same passage in up to three lengths. Each output shows one (`prefer:`); a `variant` fit remedy
can switch to a shorter one. The names are fixed.

```markdown
:::: {! variants}
::: {! variant=full}
Download the release archive for your platform, then verify its checksum.
:::
::: {! variant=short}
Download the archive and verify it.
:::
::::
```

### Links between pages

Give a page `id: jdeps` in its front matter, then link to it from any file: `[the jdeps
chapter](#jdeps)`. `[](#jdeps)` uses the page's title as the text. In a web site, the link is
rewritten to the page's file.

### Images

An image's path is written to the output unchanged, so it must be relative to the **output file**,
not to the Markdown file. Paperband doesn't copy images.

### Templating

Pebble runs twice, with different delimiters:

- Pre pass, before parsing: `{{ value }}`, `{% tag %}`, `{# comment #}`
- Post pass, after every file is parsed: `[[ value ]]`, `[% tag %]`, `[# comment #]`

Variables in both passes:

- `page.<key>`: the file's front matter
- `file`: the file's path
- the manifest's `vars`, as top-level names: `{{ product }}`
- `data.<name>`: data files; `data/site.yml` is `data.site`, `data/team/members.json` is
  `data.team.members`
- `env.NAME`: only the variables the manifest's `env` lists
- `build.date`, `build.files`
- `site`: every source. In the pre pass only paths and front matter:
  `{{ site.file("intro.md").page.title }}`. In the post pass also content:
  `[% for item in site.file("glossary.md").section("terms").list.items %]`

Fenced code blocks are not templated unless the fence says `{! template}`. Inline code is. Use
`{% verbatim %}` to keep literal braces. `include` and `extends` resolve against the templates
directory.

## Layouts

A layout is `layouts/<name>.yml`. A page gets its layout from its sequence entry's `layout:`, else
the output's `layout:`, else its own front matter `layout:`, else `defaults.layout`, else the
built-in `default` (the whole file in one box). The name `page` is reserved.

```yaml
description: Free text, for people.
page: { size: A4, margin: 15mm }     # default: the manifest's defaults.page
class: chapter-page                  # extra class on the page's <section>
unplaced: warn                       # content no box takes: warn (default) | ignore | error
prefer: short                        # variant shown on pages with this layout
stylesheet: chapter.css              # CSS file beside the layout, confined to it
css: |                               # or CSS written here, confined the same way
  h1 { color: navy }
grid:                                # named areas (or stack: { gap: 6mm }, boxes one above another)
  columns: [1fr, 2fr]
  rows: [auto, 1fr]
  areas: ["title title", "intro body"]
  gap: 24px
boxes:
  - id: title                        # required; unique in the layout
    class: hero-title                # extra class on the box's <div>
    select: h1                       # a CSS selector, or rest
    pick: first                      # first | last | N (1-based); default: every match
    scope: page                      # page (this file) | sequence | sources
    as: html                         # html | text | list | links
    area: title                      # with a grid: required, the area it goes in
    at: { x: 15mm, y: 15mm, w: 180mm, h: 30mm }   # or a fixed position (paged output only)
    wrap: true                       # false: no <div> around the content
    when: { not-empty: true }        # leave the box out when it has nothing to show
  - id: body
    select: rest                     # whatever no other box took
```

Selectors run against a tree built from the Markdown:

```html
<article>
  <section class="h1" id="intro">        <!-- a heading and everything up to the next heading -->
    <h1>Intro</h1>                       <!--   of the same or a higher level; sections nest -->
    <p>Text with <em>, <strong>, <code>, <a href>, <img src></p>
    <section class="h2" id="details">...</section>
  </section>
</article>
```

- Block elements: `h1`-`h6`, `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `blockquote`, `pre` (class `language-x`),
  `hr`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`, `div` (fenced divs), `span` (`[text]{! tag}`).
- Section ids are heading slugs: lower case, punctuation dropped, spaces to hyphens.
- Marker classes, ids and `data-*` values appear on the elements.
- Selecting a section selects its heading and all its content. `section.h1 > p` is the paragraphs
  directly under the first-level heading.
- Content is placed once. When an element and something inside it both match, the outer one wins.

Other kinds of box:

```yaml
  - { id: label, text: Contents }                    # fixed text
  - { id: file, content: path }                      # the page's file path
  - { id: md, content: source, stage: original }     # the page's Markdown: original | pre | final
  - { id: level, value: level }                      # a front matter value
  - { id: title, value: title, heading: 1 }          # ... as an <h1>
  - { id: toc, select: h1, pick: first, scope: sequence, as: links }   # a contents list
  - { id: card, select: "#summary", layout: card }   # the selection through another layout
  - id: steps                                        # one inner layout per match
    each: ".step"
    boxes:                                           # or layout: step-card
      - { id: title, select: h3 }
      - { id: text, select: rest }
```

`when` conditions: `{ page: { draft: true } }` (front matter), `{ not-empty: true }`,
`{ outputs: [pdf] }` (output names).

CSS in a layout is confined to it. `&` is the layout's own element: `& > .box-title h1 { ... }`.
Boxes have the classes `box` and `box-<id>`; the page has `layout-<name>`. A layout's CSS can't
style `html`, `body` or `:root`, and can't use `@import`.

A layout can start from another:

```yaml
extends: split
grid: { columns: [2fr, 1fr], areas: ["title title", "body intro"] }
boxes:
  intro: { class: aside }            # change a box by id; null removes it
add:
  - { id: note, area: note, text: "A note." }
```

The same keys under `layout:` in a file's front matter give that one file an inline layout.

Web output flows the boxes in order, or into the grid, and ignores `page` and `at`.

## Paged output: fitting and splitting

In `paged-html` and `pdf`, a layout with a grid, a stack or any `at:` box makes a page of fixed
size. Every box is measured. A box whose content is bigger than the box is a problem, and any
problem fails the build, which then writes `<output>.fit.html` showing each one.

Give boxes rules for what to do:

```yaml
boxes:
  - id: body
    area: body
    select: rest
    priority: normal                 # essential (default) | normal | optional
    size: { min: 120mm }             # and/or max
    split:                           # continue on further pages; split: true for the defaults
      between: section.h2            # where it may break (default: between its blocks)
      keep-together: [pre]           # never break inside these
      repeat: "h2:first-of-type"     # repeated at the top of each continuation
      continue: body-continued       # layout for continuation pages (default: this one)
    fit:                             # tried in order, measuring after each
      - shrink: { min: 90% }         # text as large as fits, never below min (default 85%)
      - tighten: true                # less line height and space between blocks
      - variant: next                # a shorter variant, where the content has one
      - drop: optional               # leave out {! optional} blocks
      - truncate: { lines: 12 }      # cut the text
fit:                                 # the page's own, when its boxes have nothing left
  - layout: chapter-compact          # lay the page out again with another layout
```

A layout with no grid, stack or `at:` flows onto as many sheets as it needs and never has a fit
problem. Use that for ordinary long documents; use fixed layouts for slides, covers and forms.

Without the `chromium` module, `pdf` is an error and `paged-html` is written unmeasured.

## Web sites

A `web` output with more than one page is a site: the first page at `file`, every other page
beside it at its source's path with `.md` replaced by `.html`, sharing `site.css` and `site.js`.
`nav: side` puts the contents beside every page; `nav: top` makes a bar of dropdowns; `nav: none`
has neither. The navigation is the page named by `contents:` (a source file or a layout name), by
default the page whose layout is `contents`; that page is then not a page of its own. Without
one, the navigation lists every page.

A contents page for `nav: top` groups its links under headings; a heading's label is the text
before its colon:

```markdown
# Contents

- [Start here](#docs-01-intro-md)

## Part 1: Basics

- [Install](#docs-02-install-md)
```

A page's id is its path with `/` and `.` replaced by `-`, or its front matter `id`.

## Themes

`theme: forest` selects a bundled theme; `theme: themes/mine` a directory. A directory with a
bundled theme's name, beside the manifest, wins.

Bundled themes: `default` (used when `theme` is absent) and `forest`.

A theme directory. Everything is optional:

```
themes/mine/
  theme.css      # added after the parts below: set variables, add rules
  web.css        # each of these replaces the built-in part of the same name
  paged.css
  content.css
  site.css
  nav-side.css
  nav-top.css
  layouts/       # layouts the theme supplies; a project's layout of the same name wins
  fonts/         # files theme.css refers to
```

Any other `.css` file in the directory is an error. A `url("fonts/x.woff2")` naming a file inside
the theme is embedded in the output as a data URL, which is how a theme's fonts reach the PDF.

Variables the built-in styles read, to set in `theme.css` on `:root`:

- both: `--pb-font-body`, `--pb-font-code`, `--pb-code-bg`, `--pb-table-rule`, `--pb-tok-*`
- web: `--pb-rule`, `--pb-page-width`, `--pb-grid-width`, `--pb-link`
- paged: `--pb-fg`, `--pb-page-bg`, `--pb-desk-bg`

The body has class `web` or `paged`, so one file can style each: `body.web h1 { ... }`.

Styles apply in this order, later ones overriding: theme parts, `theme.css`, the manifest's
`stylesheets`, each layout's CSS.

### The forest theme

White pages, one deep-green accent (`#2F5D50`), Source Sans 3 with light headlines. It adds two
classes for any page:

```markdown
Section label {! label}

# The title

A footer line {! footer}
```

and eight slide layouts on a 254mm x 142.875mm (10in x 5.625in) page. Each slide is one Markdown
file. Text must be short: these are fixed boxes, and overflow fails the build.

| Layout | Content it takes |
| --- | --- |
| `title-photo` | `p.label`, `h1`, one paragraph under it (subtitle), an image, `p.footer` |
| `statement-photo` | `p.label`, `h1` or `blockquote` (the statement), an image, `p.footer` |
| `list-photo` | `p.label`, `h1`, one `ul` or `ol`, an image, `p.footer` |
| `three-columns` | `p.label`, `h1`, three `##` sections, each a heading and short text |
| `four-steps` | `p.label`, `h1`, four `##` sections |
| `title-content` | `p.label`, `h1`, anything else as the body, `p.footer` |
| `section` | `p.label`, `h1`; solid green divider |
| `closing-photo` | `p.label`, `h1`, one paragraph under it, an image, `p.footer` |

A slide:

```markdown
---
layout: three-columns
---
How it is used {! label}

# One theme, three kinds of output

## Web

A flowing page or a whole site.

## Print

Fixed pages, measured before they ship.

## Slides

The same content on a 16:9 canvas.
```

A deck's manifest:

```yaml
title: My deck
theme: forest
sources: [slides/*.md]
sequence:
  - files: slides/*.md
outputs:
  - { name: deck, format: pdf, file: target/deck.pdf }
```

## Diagrams

With the `mermaid` or `plantuml` module added as a plugin dependency (same group and version as
`chromium`), fenced blocks in those languages are drawn as inline SVG at build time. A diagram
that can't be drawn fails the build.

## Mistakes that stop a build

- A key this guide doesn't list. Unknown keys are errors everywhere.
- A marker in the wrong place, such as mid-sentence after a space. Inline markers touch the
  element they tag: `[Save]{! ui}`.
- `layout:` naming a layout that doesn't exist in `layouts/` or the theme.
- A grid layout where a box has no `area`, or an area isn't a rectangle.
- `size: 16:9` without quotes.
- A `pdf` output without the `chromium` plugin dependency.
- Content too long for a fixed box, with no `fit:` or `split:` rule to handle it.
- `files` together with `sources` or `sequence`; `output` together with `outputs`; an output's
  `layout` together with its `layouts`.
- `nav`, `contents` or `single` on an output that isn't `web`.
- An image path written relative to the Markdown file instead of the output file.
- A link to `#an-id` that no page or element has. It warns, and fails with `failOnWarnings`.
